title: Alternative Text and Image Meaning
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of alternative text and image meaning in a browser document.
Apply at least one relevant rule from this lesson to a small HTML example.
Check the result using browser inspection, a validator, or an accessibility checklist.

content.intro: This lesson turns “Alternative Text and Image Meaning” into a practical authoring skill. You will work with writing useful alternative text, understand the choices that matter, and check the result instead of relying on guesswork.
content.why_it_matters: Text, links, lists, images, and media are the building blocks of readable, navigable web content; the markup should communicate meaning even before CSS is added.

content_blocks.title: Alternative Text and Image Meaning concept map
content_blocks.alt_text: A concept map for Alternative Text and Image Meaning, connecting the core idea, key concepts, a relevant example, and a verification step.
content_blocks.caption: Use the example and expected result to check your understanding of Alternative Text and Image Meaning.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Text, links, lists, images, and media are the building blocks of readable, navigable web content; the markup should communicate meaning even before CSS is added.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Write alternative text for the image’s purpose in context: describe meaningful information or function, use alt="" for decoration, and avoid repeating nearby text.

items.title: Functional images used as links or buttons
items.text: Resolve the URL relative to the current document or base URL. Prefer meaningful link text, test internal paths from each page location, and verify external destinations.

items.title: Complex images and longer descriptions
items.text: Metadata describes the document or its relationship to other resources. Keep each value accurate, unique where appropriate, and consistent with the visible page; search systems may ignore metadata that is misleading.

items.title: Image captions and nearby context
items.text: Include the media controls people need and alternatives to important audio or visual information. Check format support, file paths, caption timing, and permission/privacy needs.

items.title: Avoiding redundant alternative text
items.text: Write alternative text for the image’s purpose in context: describe meaningful information or function, use alt="" for decoration, and avoid repeating nearby text.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Prefer the native semantic element that communicates intent. Do not choose markup solely for its default visual style.

content.task: Create a small HTML example that demonstrates alternative text and image meaning. Keep the markup minimal, give every element a clear purpose, and inspect the rendered result.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the relevant concept from Alternative Text and Image Meaning.
Keep IDs unique and use valid nesting.
Check the result in a browser and record one finding.
hints: Start with the smallest valid example for alternative text and image meaning.
Add one element or attribute at a time, then check the result.
Compare the source and rendered DOM if the behavior surprises you.
content.expected_output: A structured article with a top-level heading, a subsection, and meaningful emphasis.

troubleshooting.symptom: The expected content does not appear.
troubleshooting.check: Confirm the file was saved with an .html extension and inspect its path and nesting.
Check the resolved URL and confirm the referenced file or external resource exists and allows the request.

troubleshooting.symptom: The page looks correct but the markup may be invalid.
troubleshooting.check: Run the Nu Html Checker and follow its first relevant diagnostic, then validate again.

common_mistakes.why: The default appearance is not the element’s main meaning and can make navigation or maintenance harder.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose the element that matches the content purpose, then use CSS for presentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a browser’s recovery means the source is valid
common_mistakes.why: Browsers often recover from malformed markup, which can hide defects and produce unexpected document structure.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the rendered DOM and run a validator against the original source.

common_mistakes.why: Missing files, narrow viewports, keyboard access, invalid input, or other states can expose defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected state plus one realistic edge case and an accessibility path.

summary: Alternative Text and Image Meaning is about expressing document structure or behavior intentionally.
Write alternative text for the image’s purpose in context: describe meaningful information or function, use alt="" for decoration, and avoid repeating nearby text.
Verify both markup and behavior; do not infer correctness from appearance alone.
